problem: Lack of evaluation resources for fan-out multi-hop, multi-document reasoning questions that require finding information about a large number of entities, hindering assessment of LLMs' reasoning over inter-document dependencies.
method: Introduces FanOutQA, a high-quality dataset of fan-out question-answer pairs with human-annotated decompositions, using English Wikipedia as the knowledge base. Defines three benchmark settings across the dataset and evaluates seven LLMs (GPT-4, LLaMA 2, Claude-2.1, Mixtral-8x7B, etc.) to measure reasoning over inter-document dependencies in long context.
key_assumptions: Fan-out questions require multi-document reasoning and can be effectively evaluated using a Wikipedia-based dataset.
Human-annotated decompositions aid in assessing reasoning steps.
main_contribution: FanOutQA benchmark dataset and open-source evaluation tools to assess LLM reasoning on complex multi-hop, multi-document questions, revealing that current LLMs still have room for improvement in inter-document dependency reasoning.
benchmarks: Three benchmark settings on FanOutQA (specific settings not detailed in abstract)
baselines: GPT-4, LLaMA 2, Claude-2.1, Mixtral-8x7B, and other LLMs (unspecified count)
results: ["Contemporary models still have room to improve reasoning over inter-document dependencies in long context."]

relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: FanOutQA provides a benchmark for evaluating LLM reasoning on fan-out questions, while the idea focuses on training LMs with enriched context subgraphs, adaptive repair loops, and RL transfer to improve multi-hop KGQA performance.
